title: Stock Market Update: Trump-Xi Ceasefire Provides Some Market Relief
text:
Trump-Xi Ceasefire Provides Some Market Relief 03-Dec-18 13:00 ET Dow +227.90 at 25765.26, Nasdaq +84.55 at 7415.29, S&P +21.82 at 2782.26
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 is up 0.8% after some relief that the trade relationship between the U.S. and China did not worsen over weekend. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 0.9%, the Nasdaq Composite is up 1.2%, and the Russell 2000 is up 0.4%.
 the next It was previously speculated that this would be the outcome. With nothing settled in terms of the major issues, though, there has been some selling into the early strength over a possible market overreaction.
Outperforming the broader market today are the consumer discretionary (+2.0%), energy (+1.8%), information technology (+1.4%), and the trade-sensitive industrial (+1.2%) and material (+1.2%) sectors.
Amazon (AMZN 1767.54, +77.31) has extended its impressive performance from last week with a gain of 4.6% today to help carry the consumer discretionary sector. The company has entered a three-horse race between Apple (AAPL 182.08, +3.54, +2.0%) and Microsoft (MSFT 111.81, +0.92, +0.8%) to be the world's largest company by market cap.
Within energy, stocks have risen in tandem with WTI crude up 3.2% to $52.57/bbl. Crude was up as much 5.7% overnight, as traders responded favorably to news of the Trump-Xi agreement and the province of Alberta's decision to cut production by 325,000 barrels per day to help curtail excess supply. There was also some surprising news that Qatar plans to withdraw from OPEC to focus on gas production.
Chip stocks have had a great day, as well, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 2.3%. Advanced Micro (AMD 23.32, +2.03) and NVIDIA (NVDA 168.44, +4.99) have had strong performances with respective gains of 9.4% and 3.0%.
On the other hand, the defensive-oriented health care (+0.1%), real estate (-0.3%), and consumer staples (-0.5%) sectors have underperformed the broader market thus far.
In M&A news, pharmaceutical company Tesaro (TSRO 73.50, +27.12) has soared 58.5% after agreeing to be acquired by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK 38.70, -3.18, -7.6%) for roughly $5.1 billion. Also, Tribune Media (TRCO 44.22, +3.96) is up 9.8% after Nexstar (NXST 84.48, +1.86, +2.3%) has agreed to acquire have turned positive after some early selling, pushing yields lower. The benchmark 10-yr yield is down two basis points to 2.99%, and the U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.3% to 96.95. The early selling in the Treasury market didn't match the level of early enthusiasm in the stock market, highlighting a more practical awareness in the fixed-income market that a trade solution.
